The [course map](../examples.qmd) links every implemented AEDT family lesson. This page owns exact specifications and failure rules, and the [current formats](#current-formats) this version reads.

The Solid/Thin-Film modeling extension below does not revise the v2
transaction or Q3D v3 contracts except where this page explicitly
describes the required 3D modeling selection.

## One shared lifecycle

SCGSim owns one portable AEDT lifecycle:

```text
PDK geometry and material identities
-> immutable handoff
-> explicit local execution
-> native AEDT readback
-> hashed receipt
-> strict result resolution
```

SCGSim supports AEDT 2023.2 and 2024.2 with the same
PyAEDT 1.3.0 pin. It copies all required inputs, opens a new local AEDT Desktop
only on explicit execution, saves and releases the owned project, and fails
closed on missing native evidence or result bytes. The package permits Python
3.12 and 3.13 with this unchanged PyAEDT pin; interpreter compatibility and
native AEDT expression correctness are separate claims.

### Explicit AEDT version selection {#aedt-version-selection}

Every new AEDT-native preparation, execution, or saved-field analysis request
and every handoff requires the `aedt_version` keyword with exactly `"2023.2"`
or `"2024.2"`. Missing or unsupported values fail before PyAEDT
import or Desktop construction. There is no default and no fallback between
releases. The selector is transaction-local; both releases use the existing
transaction owner and run profile, and the selected AEDT Desktop runs on the
same node as SCGSim.

For AEDT 2023.2, PyAEDT 1.3.0 is configured for the same-node gRPC
compatibility path with `use_grpc_api=True`, `grpc_secure_mode=False`,
`grpc_local=True`, and `grpc_listen_all=False`. The transaction sets
`PYAEDT_USE_PRE_GRPC_ARGS="True"` for that operation. It snapshots and restores
the prior transport environment through owned Desktop release, including
failure cleanup. AEDT 2024.2 uses no transport overrides. A 2023.2 request is
never downgraded or silently redirected to 2024.2, and the contract adds no
remote Desktop or scheduler execution path.

Saved source origin, the requested AEDT version, and the actual connected AEDT
version are distinct. If a saved artifact has no recorded origin, its origin
remains `None`; analysis is allowed and does not require recovering that
historical fact. SCGSim does not look up, guess, or migrate an unknown origin.
The explicit request selects the local runtime, while the actual version comes
from the connected AEDT application rather than from the request value.
PDK superconductors lower to PEC without replacing their source-material
identity. Native HFSS solids use the `pec` material with Solve Inside disabled;
native HFSS sheets use the `SCGSimPEC` Perfect E boundary. Completion requires
fresh native object-type, material or boundary-type, assignment, and complete
face-coverage readback. Other materials reference exact PDK-provided AEDT
library names; SCGSim does not invent numeric material properties.

The public lifecycle has one transaction owner and three private family
pipelines:

```text
run.py: validate cohort -> write running receipt -> own Desktop -> dispatch
family: prepare native model -> solve explicit setup -> export/read back
run.py: release Desktop -> write final receipt
```

The normal command and preparation-only paths use the same private family
preparation functions and transaction owner. EPR and Q3D already support
`--execute --prepare-only`; the Solid/Thin-Film scope extends that operation
to HFSS Eigenmode and Driven Terminal. The usual `--execute`
family behavior remains unchanged, and neither path creates a second Desktop
owner.

### Model-only preparation and physics resolution {#aedt-model-only-preparation}

The public geometry-preparation helpers for Q3D, HFSS Eigenmode, and HFSS
Driven, and `EigenmodeSim.set_eigenmode()`, accept `run_control=None` when the
request is to build and read back the native model without solving. The
canonical JSON spec still contains its `run_control` member; `null` is the
explicit model-only value. Existing non-null payload encoding and hash meaning
are unchanged. With `null`, preparation creates no solver setup, EPR cache, or
frequency sweep. It constructs the requested model and assignments, saves the
project, releases the owned Desktop, and records the actual preparation
readback.

Supplying complete run controls still authors the requested setup when
execution is preparation-only. `--prepare-only` selects the execution stage;
it does not remove or invent request controls. A solve request without complete
controls fails before opening AEDT. A no-analysis, model-only `HfssEprSpec`
carrier accepts `run_control=None`. An EPR analysis/cache request requires
complete Eigenmode controls; `run_control=None` cannot be used to skip its
setup.

A successful model-only handoff records the `native_preparation_only` stage.
`resolve_prepared_model(run_dir)` returns a `PreparedModel` from that saved
handoff and its native preparation/readback evidence. This reader reports the
prepared-model stage; it does not report a completed physics result.
`resolve_results()` remains the strict reader for completed solver results and
does not treat a model-only receipt as a completed solve.

## Prepared-native HFSS EPR batch {#prepared-native-hfss-epr-batch}

Use this workflow for a complete, released HFSS EPR preparation when the
solver-only process must run separately from the local PyAEDT transaction.
The preparation must include its bound source and project, setup and cache
readback, and native calculator-definition evidence. Packaging does not open
Desktop or alter the authored model, setup, margins, modes, or EPR criteria.

For a complete multi-model procedure, follow [Parameter sweep with a Desktop-free HPC solver](../course/aedt-hpc-sweep.qmd). It creates one native package per model, transports them in one ordinary archive, and collects each returned attempt separately. The outer archive and serial loop are caller composition; the public batch API continues to own one model per package.

The public Python entry points are:

```python
def prepare_native_batch(
    prepared_run: str | Path,
    *,
    output_dir: str | Path,
    solver_executable: str,
    resources: AedtResources,
    dependencies: Sequence[str] = (),
) -> NativeBatchPackage: ...

def run_native_batch(package_dir: str | Path, *, output_dir: str | Path) -> Path: ...

def collect_native_batch(
    package_dir: str | Path,
    attempt_dir: str | Path,
    *,
    output_dir: str | Path,
) -> ResolvedRun: ...
```

`NativeBatchPackage` returns `root`, `manifest_path`, and `archive_path`;
`run_native_batch` returns the path to `batch-attempt.json`.

`prepare_native_batch` accepts only a completed prepare-only HFSS EPR handoff
with serialized saved setup/cache evidence and calculator definitions read
back. A pending cache marker does not establish saved setup/cache readback.
Packaging retains the complete shared CLC artifact and verifies its recorded
status, path, byte size, and SHA-256. It starts with the required expression
definitions and follows their named-helper references; every required root and
helper must be present with a consistent definition. Missing or conflicting
required definitions fail. Unreferenced extra definitions may remain in the
shared file. If an aggregate is supplied, it must cover the required roots and
agree on shared definitions, but need not be an exclusive inventory of the
file. These checks do not rewrite the original receipt. The package contains
the source/spec and handoff
evidence, native project, calculator evidence, declared dependencies, and the
full `.aedtresults` directory when present. A dependency path is relative to
the prepared run.
For this batch recipe, `cores` must be a positive integer and
`ram_limit_percent` must be an integer from 1 through 99; 100 is not
representable by the native machine-list syntax. The `solver_executable` value
is recorded for the solver host and need not resolve on the packaging host.

`run_native_batch` copies the packaged project into a fresh attempt directory
and starts one solver process. It uses the bound executable and prepared
design/setup with AEDT's one-host `-ng -UseElectronicsPPE -distributed -auto`
BatchSolve recipe and a machine entry of
`list=<host>:-1:<cores>:<ram_limit_percent>%`. It does not import PyAEDT,
construct Desktop, submit a scheduler job, retry, or accept arbitrary solver
arguments. The RAM percentage is the native per-host solver limit; it is not
an operating-system memory cap. The attempt retains its process return code
and raw solver output. Neither a zero exit code nor a frequency CSV alone
establishes a completed result.

`collect_native_batch` requires the matching settled attempt, returned `.aedt`
project, and complete `.aedtresults` directory. It verifies the required CLC
roots and named-helper closure, plus any supplied aggregate, against the package records, then
opens an owned copy through the existing transaction and collects full
adaptive mode/pass cache history and saved-field EPR without rebuilding
geometry or running Analyze. It releases Desktop, seals the run, and applies
the strict result resolver. Missing native history or saved-field evidence
remains a failure; LastAdaptive-only data does not replace the complete cache.

The package and collection commands use `python -m scgsim.aedt.batch` in the
SCGSim environment. Each stage writes to a fresh output directory:

```sh
python -m scgsim.aedt.batch package \
  --prepared-run "$PREPARED_RUN" --output "$PACKAGE_DIR" \
  --solver-executable "$AEDT_SOLVER" --cores "$AEDT_CORES" \
  --ram-limit-percent "$AEDT_RAM_LIMIT_PERCENT"

python -m scgsim.aedt.batch solve \
  --package "$PACKAGE_DIR" --output "$ATTEMPT_DIR"

python -m scgsim.aedt.batch collect \
  --package "$PACKAGE_DIR" --attempt "$ATTEMPT_DIR" \
  --output "$COLLECTED_RUN_DIR"
```

The package stage requires `--prepared-run`, `--output`,
`--solver-executable`, `--cores`, and `--ram-limit-percent`; `--dependency`
may be repeated. The solve stage takes `--package` and `--output`. Collection
takes `--package`, `--attempt`, and `--output`.

The package archive contains the immutable package and standalone
`run_batch.py`. Transfer and extract it to the solver host using the operator's
separate transfer and job controls. Run the copied script there; it uses only
Python's standard library, so that host does not need SCGSim or PyAEDT:

```sh
python "$PACKAGE_DIR/run_batch.py" solve \
  --package "$PACKAGE_DIR" --output "$ATTEMPT_DIR"
```

The solver executable path is resolved on that host. Return the full package
and attempt to the collection host, including the returned `.aedt` project,
complete `.aedtresults` directory, attempt record, and raw solver output.
Collect from those returned directories; a frequency-only export is
insufficient.

Each family binds its request once before native preparation. The private bound
request fixes the absolute run workspace and a detached immutable spec payload;
relative spec paths remain relative to that workspace across later `chdir`,
while absolute source paths retain their lexical identity. Family preparation
parses only the bound payload, then returns a carrier containing the native app
handle and detached preparation readback. Solve and export accept only that
carrier. Export helpers work on separate copies, so helper failure or mutation
of a returned result cannot alter the preparation evidence retained by the
carrier.

Project names have two explicit representations. Direct Python authoring keeps
the existing filename normalization: a supplied filename loses its final
suffix. The canonical JSON payload stores the already-normalized project name,
so parsing and serializing that payload repeatedly preserves it byte-for-byte,
including internal dots and text that itself ends in `.aedt`. Handoff
preparation copies that canonical name unchanged and binds only the copied GDS
path in its independent payload. It does not reinterpret old truncated names,
rewrite existing artifacts, or provide a legacy-name fallback.

## Current formats and older results {#current-formats}

SCGSim reads only the formats it writes. A handoff, receipt, request or result
written by an earlier SCGSim is read with the SCGSim commit that wrote it; this
version does not convert or migrate it.

Run folders of the native AEDT builder, which this version no longer has
(issue #67), are not read: `execute_handoff`, `resolve_results()` and
`analyze_epr()` refuse their handoffs, requests and saved solutions, and the
message says to prepare and run the study again with this version. A request
whose payload carries `geometry` (the native builder's), a v1 HFSS handoff of
the GDS-import route, and a source record without `sgb_model_sha256` and
`sgb_model_files` are each refused this way.

| Record | Current format |
|---|---|
| Handoff metadata | `scgsim.aedt.handoff.v1` for Q2D and Q3D; `scgsim.aedt.handoff.v2` for HFSS Driven Terminal, Eigenmode and EPR |
| Handoff manifest | `scgsim.aedt.handoff-manifest.v1` and `.v2`, paired with the handoff above |
| Receipt | `scgsim.aedt.receipt.v3`, initial and completed |
| Runtime source | `scgsim.aedt.runtime-source.v30` ([rule](#runtime-source)) |
| HFSS EPR request | `scgsim.aedt.hfss-eigenmode-epr.v2`; `.v3` with one expression-cache convergence control, `.v4` with a collection |
| Saved-field analysis request | `scgsim.aedt.hfss-eigenmode-epr-analysis.v2`; `.v3` with surface field selectors |
| EPR result and mode-energy row | `scgsim.aedt.epr-result.v2` and `scgsim.aedt.epr-mode-energy.v2` |
| Saved-solution manifest and receipt | `scgsim.aedt.saved-solution-manifest.v2` and `scgsim.aedt.saved-solution-receipt.v2` |

Every HFSS 3D and Q3D request carries explicit `modeling` and the SGB model it
was prepared from, in its handoff's `model/` folder; the physical interpretation
is inside the model. A surface contribution always records `loss_tangent`, `source` and
`preset`, and an EPR analysis request always records `bulk_domain_ids`.

Every receipt reader (execution, `resolve_results()` and the prepared-model
reader) first checks the receipt schema and the schema of each runtime-source
record it carries. A receipt `scgsim.aedt.receipt.v1` or `.v2`, or a V3 receipt
whose runtime source has an earlier schema, is refused with a message saying
it was written by an earlier SCGSim and naming how to read it. This check comes
before any request or result is read, so an old result is refused by this one
rule rather than by whichever older format it would reach next. A v1 EPR
result or a v1 saved-solution manifest read on its own is refused with the same
message.

A new handoff writes `expected_receipt_schema: scgsim.aedt.receipt.v3` into its
metadata and manifest, and its initial V3 receipt contains
`prepared_runtime_source`, the [runtime source](#runtime-source) of the code
that prepared it. Before writing `running`, the shared transaction requires a
V3 receipt with both V3 expectation markers, a canonical manifest and the
current runtime source. Every new Q3D or HFSS 3D execution requires explicit
`modeling`; a `thin_film` request also needs its corresponding source
declarations before receipt mutation.

The verified initial-receipt hash and prepared-manifest hash are copied into
the mutable V3 receipt as `preparation_cohort: prepared_v3`. The final receipt
is intentionally not compared with its initial hash because execution must
mutate it. Unknown versions, mixed or partial markers, noncanonical members,
and hash mismatches reject before receipt mutation.

Every completed receipt has a separate `runtime_source` record, with stage
`actual`, for the code that executed it. `resolve_results()` verifies the exact
cohort, markers, canonical prepared manifest, initial-receipt binding and
complete actual runtime manifest before applying the family result checks;
HFSS completion requires sealed native PEC binding evidence. These unsigned
consistency checks do not authenticate an artifact set against an actor able
to rewrite every member.

A pure initial-receipt codec owns the exact V3 member order, two-space JSON
indentation, and the trailing newline; prepared provenance sits between
`source` and `outputs`.

### Runtime source {#runtime-source}

The runtime source names the SCGSim source files an AEDT run is made of and the
SHA-256 of each. It is computed on each use, not frozen: the static import
closure of every module under `scgsim/aedt` and of the two AEDT visualization
loaders, `scgsim/visualization/loaders/aedt.py` and `aedt_receipt.py`. The walk
follows every `import` and `from ... import` that names an `scgsim` module,
including imports inside functions, and adds each package initializer on the
way. A file elsewhere in `src` that AEDT does not import is not listed, so
moving, renaming or deleting it does not affect AEDT preparation or execution.

A record has five fields:

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `schema_version` | `scgsim.aedt.runtime-source.v30` |
| `stage` | `prepared` when the handoff is written, `actual` when execution starts |
| `modules` | one `module`, `path` and `sha256` per file, in path order |
| `content_sha256` | SHA-256 of the canonical JSON of `modules` |
| `revision_observation` | an object: `{"status": "available", "revision": "<40-hex Git commit>"}`, or `{"status": "unavailable"}` (for example a wheel without VCS metadata) |

A reader accepts a record when all of these hold:

- `schema_version` is the current one and `stage` is the one expected;
- the paths are sorted and unique, each lies under `src/scgsim/` without `..`,
  and each `module` is the dotted name of its path;
- the paths include `src/scgsim/__init__.py` and `src/scgsim/aedt/__init__.py`.
  Every AEDT import passes through both package initializers, so a list without
  either is not an AEDT closure, and they stay in place when modules move
  inside `scgsim/aedt`;
- `content_sha256` matches the recorded `modules`;
- `revision_observation` is exactly `{"status": "unavailable"}`, or an object with the two keys `status` (`"available"`) and `revision` (a 40-hex commit).

The reader does not compare the recorded hashes with the installed package:
they state which bytes ran, and the installed code may since differ. An
`unavailable` revision does not fail the record.

A record with an earlier schema, `runtime-source.v1` to `v29`, is refused with
a message saying it was written by an earlier SCGSim. Read such a result with
the SCGSim commit that wrote it; its `revision_observation` names that commit
when Git was available. Every receipt or handoff written before
`runtime-source.v30` carries an earlier schema.

Execution computes the `actual` record inside the receipt-bound failure
transaction, before importing PyAEDT or constructing Desktop. A missing source
file or a damaged record yields a failed V3 receipt without a Desktop launch
rather than escaping receipt finalization. The `prepared` and `actual` records
are evidence taken at different times and need not be equal.

The family save contract remains fail-closed. `save_project()` returning false
before solve aborts before native execution; returning false after export aborts
before completion is reported. SCGSim does not turn either state into a new
partial-success receipt or infer that native project bytes are usable.

## Solver-specific contracts

The following semantics remain separate even though they share packaging,
version checks, receipts, and path/hash validation. The table describes
solve-bearing requests and their returned physics data. Model-only preparation
uses the separate `run_control=None` path described above.

| Family | Required model semantics | Required returned data |
|---|---|---|
| HFSS Driven Terminal | an SGB model of explicit `modeling="solid"` or `modeling="thin_film"` whose two `LumpedTerminalPort`s sit on its port sheets, with explicit signal/reference identity ([below](#hfss-driven-terminal-sgb)); complete `HfssRunControl` for solving | ordered terminal S-parameters and Touchstone |
| HFSS Driven Modal | waits for its ports on the SGB model ([issue #135](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/135)); `prepare_sgb_model` refuses a `ModalPort` | none |
| HFSS Eigenmode | an SGB model of explicit `modeling="solid"` or `modeling="thin_film"`; port-free; complete `EigenmodeRunControl`, including mode count and search frequency, for solving; generic RLC model elements are distinct from `PlanarJunction` and EPR junction records | ordinary real mode frequency, native Q, and convergence evidence; EPR history and saved-field results use their separate result contract |
| Q3D | an SGB model of explicit `modeling="solid"` or `modeling="thin_film"`; exact conductor Net membership; C/G only, with no terminals (AC/RL is designed again in [issue #265](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/265)); optional exact six-face Region ground seal; complete family controls for solving | native capacitance/conductance matrix |
| Q2D | explicit cross-section geometry and conductor/reference assignments | per-unit-length capacitance/conductance and resistance/inductance matrices |

### Lumped port sheets and terminal RLC {#hfss-shared-lumped-support}

`LumpedRlc` and `LumpedTerminalPort` name a `port_sheet_id`: a port sheet of
the plan, which the SGB model carries as the `PORT::<port_sheet_id>` group, as
Palace's lumped elements do (issue #67 decision 8). There is no separate
support record. `prepare_sgb_model()` binds each one to its group and refuses
a name the model has no group for, and a port sheet that a junction, an RLC
or a lumped port share. In HFSS every port sheet must carry a junction, an
RLC or a lumped Terminal port.

The HFSS import puts each `LumpedRlc` on its port face the same way as a
junction: one Lumped RLC on the imported faces, with the current line joining
the midpoints of those faces' own edges at both ends along the sidecar
`direction`.

The SGB flow refuses a Driven wave `TerminalPort` and a Driven Modal port, with
a message naming NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim#135; until that Issue lands, AEDT Driven
wave and modal runs are not available.

AEDT keeps only `[A-Za-z0-9_]` of a name, so a Net's AEDT name (its Q3D Net
and its HFSS `perfect_e_<name>` boundary) is its ID with every other
character replaced by `_`. `prepare_sgb_model()` refuses two Nets whose IDs
become the same name, such as `chip/A` and `chip_A`, naming both Net IDs and
the shared name, before AEDT is touched; neither is renamed. The same rule
names a junction's Lumped RLC `junction_rlc_<junction_id>` and a port sheet's
`LumpedRlc` `rlc_<port_sheet_id>`: two junction IDs, or two port-sheet IDs,
whose names coincide are refused the same way, with no `__2` suffix.

A handoff of the SGB flow carries its model: the STEP, the BREP it was
written from, the sidecar and the guard are copied into the handoff's
`model/` folder, and the request names that relative folder. Where AEDT runs,
every file is checked against its recorded SHA-256 before anything is
imported. The handoff's source record binds the model's identity and the four
file hashes; a record without them belongs to a natively built model, which
is refused (issue #67 decision 6).

The EPR of an SGB model reads what it integrates from the sidecar and the
prepared record, without AEDT (`scgsim.aedt.epr.sgb_source`). The domains
are the imported dielectric solids, by AEDT object name, and the `Region`;
a conductor solid is PEC and holds no field. Each sidecar Surface-EPR row of a
declared type is integrated once, on the non-model sheet of its faces. The
reported contributions group the rows as Palace's `Dielectric` rows do: per
interface type and surface unit (an unbanded row, or every band of one band
family) a baseline over all its rows, and per inset margin an entry over its
bands from the margin's band on, under Palace's entry names; an entry's energy
is the sum of its rows'. AEDT has no Palace `Model.L0`, so a film given in
Palace's native `thickness` is refused; give `film_thickness_m`. A junction's
voltage is the area integral of the field along its port's sidecar
`direction`, divided by the port sheet's width across it, read from the
sidecar's port record; `prepare_sgb_model()` refuses a `PlanarJunction` whose
`width_um` is not that width within the model's `tolerance_um`. Each row has
three expressions on its sheet (normal and tangential electric integrals and
the area); a row can hold faces of several orientations and curved walls, so
the normal is the sheet's own at each point (`Operation('Normal')`), not one
vector. A junction's voltage is integrated on a non-model sheet copied from
its port faces. The public HFSS Eigenmode flow runs on this (see
[Eigenmode saved fields](#eigenmode-saved-fields-and-surface-epr-direction)).

In AEDT, `modeling="thin_film"` builds Route A with its finite bodies (bumps,
posts) retained as conductor solids (`ROUTE_A_RETAINED_BODIES`; the sidecar's
`route_policy.conductor_volumes` is `retained`), and the import makes them
PEC, the same way a Route B request is built as Route C. A sheet face that
such a body stands on imports on the body and on the substrate; its
Surface-EPR rows read the substrate's copy, the copy it has when the body is
excluded.

### HFSS Driven Terminal on the SGB model {#hfss-driven-terminal-sgb}

`prepare_hfss_driven_from_geometry(model=...)` prepares the Driven Terminal
handoff of a `PreparedSgbModel` whose `lumped_ports` are its two ports
(`prepare_sgb_model(..., ports=...)`). `HfssDrivenGeometrySpec` (schema
`hfss-driven-geometry.v1`, mode `terminal`) carries the model; its `ports` are
the model's. The request requires ports 1 and 2 with distinct names and one
shared ordered reference; each port sheet's two host Entities must be one of
its port's signal Entities and one of its reference Entities. A Driven model
carries no junctions, lumped RLCs or Surface-EPR specs. The handoff carries the
model's four files in `model/`, and the receipt source binds `sgb_model_sha256`
and `sgb_model_files`, as for HFSS Eigenmode. A request payload with `geometry`
(the native builder's) is refused with the reason.

In AEDT the run imports the STEP into an empty Driven Terminal design
(`import_sgb_model`), with the Region, its Perfect H and the Perfect E of each
Route A Net as for Eigenmode. A model with lumped Terminal ports is imported
only into a Driven Terminal design, and a Driven Terminal design only takes a
model that has them. Each port is then:

1. **The sheet.** A port face on an imported solid is drawn again as one sheet
   object, `port_sheet_<port_sheet_id>`, from the guard's exact vertex loop of
   each face, checked against the guard's area; a face that is not a flat
   polygon of its vertices is refused. AEDT 2024.2 imports a substrate face
   about 2e-8 um from the conductor solids beside it, too far for a Terminal
   port to find them (development check, 2026-11-15). A free face is already
   such a sheet.
2. **The port.** A Terminal `Lumped Port` named as the request names it, over
   the sheet's faces, with the request's impedance and `renormalize`.
3. **The Terminal.** `<name>_T1`, on the sheet's straight edges at the signal
   host's end along the sidecar `direction` (which points from the sheet's
   first host to its second); those edges must form one unbroken segment.
   AEDT makes a lumped port with an integration line a Modal port with no
   Terminal, even in a Driven Terminal design, so the Terminal is assigned on
   the edges.

After the save, every port is read back from the saved design: a Terminal
`Lumped Port` on exactly its faces, its one Terminal the saved child on exactly
its edges. The receipt keeps these records, the native properties and the
reference conductors AEDT records. Result reading requires the receipt's
geometry to be the request's model as imported (its identity and the guard's
solids), each port record to be the one the import made, and the ordered
S-parameters and Touchstone of the declared sweep.

`LumpedRlc` requires an explicit `series` or `parallel` topology. Its R, L and
C components are independently selected; `None` disables the corresponding
component. Each enabled generic R, L or C value must be finite after numeric
conversion. Zero remains enabled, and finite negative values are preserved.
Historical generic RLC payloads containing nonfinite values are rejected by
current constructors, including payload decoding. This restriction applies
only to these generic RLC components, not to other circuit or EPR quantities.
`EigenmodeSim.add_lumped_rlc()` adds to the model-owned collection, one
treatment per port sheet; `HfssEprSpec` only projects the prepared list and
does not introduce a second editable copy. The model-source hash includes the
RLC records. This generic linear network is not a Josephson junction and does
not create a `PlanarJunction`, junction participation, or an EPR contribution.
Existing junction and saved-field EPR result contracts remain separate.

### Family-specific setup controls {#aedt-family-setup-controls}

Public run-control models express caller intent; they do not expose a mutable
AEDT setup-property dictionary. The private family mappings translate each
typed control into that solver's native setup and saved-property readback.
The dual-version runtime contract above keeps this run-control vocabulary
unchanged under AEDT 2023.2 or 2024.2 and PyAEDT 1.3.0.

| Family | Public run control | Native setup mapping |
|---|---|---|
| HFSS Eigenmode, including EPR | `EigenmodeRunControl` | One private mapping in `scgsim.aedt.runtime.native.hfss_eigenmode` maps the seven controls to `MinimumFrequency`, `NumModes`, `MaxDeltaFreq`, `MaximumPasses`, `MinimumPasses`, `MinimumConvergedPasses`, and `PercentRefinement` for ordinary Eigenmode and EPR. |
| HFSS Driven Terminal | `HfssRunControl` | The Driven-HFSS adaptive setup and frequency sweep are translated within the HFSS family. |
| Q3D | `MatrixRunControl` | Q3D owns its `Cap` block; the `AC` and `DC` blocks stay disabled. |
| Q2D | `MatrixRunControl` | Q2D owns its `CGDataBlock` and `RLDataBlock` controls. |

The shared Q3D and Q2D request vocabulary does not make their native blocks
interchangeable. Likewise, the shared native runtime owns Desktop lifecycle,
ACF/resource handling, and access to the saved `AnalysisSetup` tree; raw
property retrieval does not interpret solver fields or replace each family's
own saved-setup reader. EPR adds its expression-cache items to the shared
Eigenmode base setup and owns that extension, not a second adaptive-field
mapping.

No family may report completion from requested PyAEDT object properties alone.
The receipt records direct AEDT state and hashes every resolved output. A
resolver rejects unsupported families, partial output, mixed run identity,
unresolved native assignments, and path/hash mismatches.
Likewise, a `completed` label and an `.aedt` file alone do not prove that saved
fields are present or reusable; only the versioned family evidence sealed and
checked by the resolver has that meaning.

## Solid and thin-film 3D modeling {#aedt-solid-thin-film}

Every fresh Q3D
or HFSS 3D request explicitly selects `modeling="solid"` or `"thin_film"`;
there is no inferred mode or public A/B/C execution alias. Current family
schema identifiers remain in use. The selection decides the SGB route the
model is built on: `thin_film` is Route A, `solid` Route C. The physical
interpretation below is applied when the model is built, and the request
carries the model, not a representation of its own. See the
[shared physical representation contract](physical-representation.qmd) for the
neutral ABI and the explicit Palace profile interface; Q2D remains a separate
cross-section contract.

The selected PDK/source declares `PhysicalLayerDeclaration` records containing
physical identity, source level/selector, source interval, material identity,
`feature_kind`, physical dimensions and authored contact facts. The feature
kinds are `stack_film`, `local_film` and `finite_volume`. The source carrier is
`physical_layer`; fresh `aedt_modeling` metadata and role-derived route
classification are retired. Classification is not inferred from names, Nets,
materials, size, proximity or equal Z values. One physical layer identity is
shared across its polygons and placed occurrences, without a separate stack
identifier. The input uses one explicitly authored LayerStack assembly frame.

Only source-selected physical levels enter the interpreted declaration set;
unused catalogue films do not collapse the model. Selected source-qualified
bridge incidence is retained as source evidence, while generic unauthored
bridge/bump contact remains missing. Neither establishes native continuity or
HFSS field-side correspondence.

An explicit `ApproximationProfile` and the common
`PhysicalRepresentationPlan` own coordinate mapping, per-body interpretation,
layer-bound support projection and the full requested enclosure. Finite volumes map their actual body endpoints rather than taking
the whole nominal layer span. Film physical thickness remains the source's
normal thickness. A TSV wall's radial thickness is not its axial span.
Explicit Solid geometry without layer declarations can use the common
identity plan without inventing physical IDs.

In `solid` mode, the model retains source physical Z intervals. In
`thin_film` mode, a stack-bearing film is represented as a sheet and its
declared thickness is removed from the cumulative stack height. The resulting
effective Z map is applied to every layer above it in that stack. A local
film/deck becomes a sheet at its declared contact side after the stack map is
applied; its own thickness does not compress the stack. A finite volume stays
three-dimensional with its actual body endpoints mapped. Posts and bumps remain solids
with mapped endpoints and receive no inferred extension. These mappings are
derived from authored declarations; there is no hard-coded layer identity or
film thickness.

Both modes preserve source XY outlines, holes, material identity, object and
Net names, and the Net-to-Objects one-to-many relationship. Geometry is not
united at the Net level. Source geometry, effective geometry, dielectric
interfaces, ports, Region placement and EPR geometry use the same effective
stack map while retaining separate source/effective provenance. Physical
source facts are not overwritten by their effective representation.

For GeometryPlan-backed lowering, a derived child's Ground identity remains
local to that source occurrence. Preserve its source outline and holes, caller
Net membership, and recorded occurrence transform; apply that transform once.
Do not infer physical Ground from a parent, Net name, or bounding box. The
physical Ground role and the solver's native Net type are separate explicit
facts.

The conductor's source normal thickness or `physical_thickness_um` is not the
interface-film thickness used by the EPR model. The `film_thickness_m` of the
MA, MS or SA spec given to `set_surface_epr()` is an independent model input. Do
not substitute the conductor thickness for that interface assumption.

An ideal superconductor is determined by the stack's material record; the
original material ID (such as Al or Nb) remains recorded. A solid maps to native `pec`. A thin Q3D body uses
`ThinConductor` with material `pec` and the declared physical thickness with
explicit units. A thin HFSS body uses `Perfect E`. Non-superconducting
dielectric and vacuum assignments use explicit PDK AEDT library mappings.
Unsupported material models fail explicitly; no room-temperature material or
loss model is substituted.

Existing HFSS mode-specific port and reference contracts remain in force under the same
coordinate map.

The existing `python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --execute --prepare-only`
operation prepares, reads back, saves and releases a model for Q3D C/G,
HFSS Eigenmode and HFSS Driven Terminal. It does not
call `Analyze`, create a solver mesh, solve, or export fields or result
matrices. Its preparation-only receipt is not a completed solve result; strict
result resolution remains unchanged. The ordinary explicit solve path remains
available, but this modeling scope does not claim a solver result or numerical
accuracy for either representation.

### HFSS Driven caller-owned sweep count {#hfss-driven-sweep-count}

`FrequencySweepSpec(start_ghz, stop_ghz, points=20000)` keeps its
existing public `points` field and default. The caller chooses the sample count
for the study. Exact whole-number numeric inputs, including `20000.0`, are
accepted and converted losslessly to the native/count integer. A non-whole
input is rejected rather than truncated. This contract adds no scientific
minimum, maximum or adequate-sampling envelope; native sweep/domain failures
retain their native meaning.

The bound count governs native sweep setup, exports and returned-data
readback/reader cardinality together. The returned frequencies and ordered
network data must belong to that request, with the existing endpoint, unit,
port-order, source/readback and hash bindings. There is no hidden 20,000-point
export or reader assumption for a differently requested count, no resampling
or interpolation, and no fallback to another sweep.

Valid historical 20,000-point data and its canonical input/receipt custody
remain valid under their existing identities. The numeric input `20000.0`
does not become an invalid historical request merely because a native API uses
an integer count. Changing the caller's count creates a different request;
it does not relabel old returned data. Q2D/Q3D behavior is unchanged by this selected count direction. The separate
HFSS convergence-observation direction below governs qualification. Sampling
adequacy remains the caller's research interpretation, not a count threshold
chosen by SCGSim.

### HFSS convergence observations {#hfss-convergence-observations}

This observation contract covers HFSS Driven and Eigenmode only. Native convergence status,
caller-authored criteria and changes, reported delta, final pass and available
native records remain observations. For Eigenmode, `Current Consecutive Passes`
and native convergence history remain in the hash-bound
`adaptive-convergence.prop` export. The parser reads and structurally checks
the count; the existing normalized result/report does not expose that count
or reproduce the full raw history. SCGSim removes only
these three additional qualification rejections:

- A native converged classification is not rejected solely because the final
  reported convergence delta exceeds the caller's configured target: maximum
  magnitude delta-S (ratio) for Driven, or frequency change (percent) for Eigenmode.
- A native not-converged classification is not rejected solely because the
  final pass differs from the caller's configured maximum.
- Eigenmode's native converged classification is not rejected solely because
  the reported consecutive-pass count is below the caller's requested minimum.

The native classification is retained with the values that accompanied it;
it does not independently certify the criterion or research adequacy. A pass
count alone does not explain why native work stopped. An unknown cause stays
unknown rather than being labeled OOM, walltime or successful early stopping.
Actual OOM/walltime interruption, native analyze/save failure and incomplete
or corrupt returned artifacts retain their genuine failure meaning. This
change does not mark failed/incomplete work completed or reclassify an old
FAILED receipt.

Request-setting identity (C4), cross-export self-consistency (C5), native/source
identity, required formats and artifact hashes remain checked. Requested
controls and returned evidence must still belong to the same run. The separate
[Q2D/Q3D observation contract](#q2d-q3d-convergence-observations) below covers
matrix-family qualifications. The caller interprets quantity/history
for the intended SCQ use as taught in the
[result-reading lesson](../course/returned-results.qmd#interpret-for-scq-use);
this direction adds no numerical sufficiency threshold or scientific certification.

### Q2D/Q3D convergence observations {#q2d-q3d-convergence-observations}

The Q2D/Q3D contract applies the native-observation direction to
these two additional qualifications, separately from the earlier HFSS-only
scope:

- A native converged classification is not rejected solely because its final
  reported delta exceeds the configured target.
- A native not-converged classification is not rejected solely because its
  completed pass count differs from the configured maximum.

Native status, target, final delta, completed passes and source remain recorded
observations. Keep the caller's actual controls and any changes with those
records when interpreting a matrix quantity for the intended study. The native
classification does not independently certify the criterion or research
adequacy. Pass count alone does not identify OOM, walltime or successful early
stopping; an unknown cause remains unknown.

Native analyze/save/export failures and missing or corrupt artifacts retain
their failure meaning; existing FAILED receipts are not reclassified. Required
metric/control formats, configured-control identity, native/source identity and
artifact custody remain checked. The Q2D one-file primary matrix
export, finite C/G/L/R data, units, frequency, conductor order and historical
readers are unchanged. This behavior changes no API/schema or numeric
precision and establishes no research threshold or scientific certification.

### HFSS Eigenmode native frequency export {#hfss-eigenmode-native-frequency-export}

The shared HFSS Eigenmode exporter accepts native real-only mode rows with
three fields (`mode`, real `frequency_ghz`, native `Q`) and complex-frequency
rows with six fields (`mode`, real frequency, `+` or `-`, imaginary magnitude,
lowercase `j`, native `Q`). The stored `frequency_ghz` is the real component.
The parser validates a finite imaginary component but does not turn it into a
damping value or calculate Q. It preserves the native Q token's numeric value.
The original `eigenmodes.eig` remains in the hashed output manifest, so the
complex component's sign and magnitude remain available as raw provenance.

The normalized `eigenmodes.csv` columns remain `mode`, `frequency_ghz`, and
`q_factor`; the `result_readback.eigenmodes` fields and receipt schema are
unchanged. Ordinary Eigenmode runs, EPR solves, and saved-field EPR analysis
share this exporter. Saved-field analysis uses the real frequency component
when evaluating each mode.

The version, design, setup, and table headers remain required. Blank and
comment lines after the table header are allowed. A noncomment body record
with an unsupported shape, nonpositive or non-ASCII-integer mode, bad
separator, invalid numeric field, nonfinite value, nonpositive real frequency,
or negative Q fails with a line-specific malformed/invalid-row error. Valid
rows must still be exactly the requested ordered modes `1..num_modes`; missing,
duplicate, or reordered mode indices fail the separate native mode
count/order check. A malformed row is therefore not reported as a missing
solver mode. These checks describe parser behavior only and do not establish a
private consumer solve or EPR result.

### Native simulation benchmark

Every new completed HFSS Driven Terminal, Eigenmode (including
EPR), Q3D, and Q2D solve writes a versioned
`results/simulation-benchmark.v1.json` during its owned AEDT session. The run
receipt names and hashes that output. Its `status` distinguishes complete
native profile data from an unavailable profile or a profile API/format error;
the latter two do not turn a successful physics solve into solver failure.
Failure to write or hash the claimed JSON is an artifact-integrity failure.
Historical completed receipts without this output remain readable and report
`not_recorded`, without synthesizing old profile measurements. A claimed but
missing or hash-mismatched benchmark is rejected by `resolve_results()`.

The benchmark preserves exact native setup, variation, solution-process group,
adaptive pass, and stage identities. It records only available native real or
elapsed and CPU times, native Memory with its formatted string and PyAEDT
conversion, and explicitly labeled tetrahedra, solved
elements, or linear matrix size. A terminal result-matrix dimension is never
called a solver matrix size. Stage peaks are maxima, not sums; parent and child
times are not added because they may overlap. Missing metrics and Q3D adaptive
profile limitations remain unavailable, never zero. SCGSim receipt wall times
stay separate from native task times. Profile capture traverses the native
`results/profile` OO tree directly so native read failures become benchmark
errors rather than silently omitted groups; it also retains scalar setup-root
properties carrying native variation identity.

Memory conversion does not establish quantity scope. The
[v242 HFSS task-profile definition](https://ansyshelp.ansys.com/public/Views/Secured/Electronics/v242/en/Subsystems/HFSS/Content/ReportsandPostProc/ViewingaSolutionProfile.htm)
defines Memory as peak physical RAM for the executable performing that task.
SCGSim qualifies a captured `results/profile` row only when its native `Name`
matches the row identity, its `Real time`, `Cpu time`, and `Memory` task columns
are present with parsed timing metrics, and it is outside the explicit HPC
resource subtree. Unqualified Memory, including HPC Machine information, retains
its native value with unknown scope; no host-capacity or usage meaning is inferred.
Stage memory peaks include only qualified task rows and remain unavailable when
none exist. They are maxima of observed task peaks, not a whole-host peak or sum.
One pure detached projection serves capture, verified offline reading, and direct
Report display. Receipt V3 and benchmark v1 carry this shared attribution leaf.

`ResolvedRun.simulation_benchmark()` retains its four existing summary keys and
adds the verified benchmark record.
`show_simulation_benchmark(show_details=False, theme="light")` returns a
notebook-displayable report with the same `.data`, summary cards,
native-stage/pass table, and Plotly adaptive-stage curves when native values are
present. When only native elapsed time exists, tables and curves label it
`elapsed` rather than presenting it as real time. Eigenmode adaptive passes,
Driven adaptive and sweep scopes, and
Q3D/Q2D native subproblem and element labels remain separate; a family without
reported adaptive values has no invented pass curve. Details optionally shows
stages and exact provenance. Rendering and offline resolution never open AEDT.
The AEDT report methods accept keyword-only `theme="light"` or `theme="dark"`,
default to light, and reject other values. `AedtBenchmarkReport` keeps its
existing `.data` and carries the selected theme.

## Q2D native combined matrix export

For new Q2D runs, the canonical result set contains exactly one matrix
artifact: `results/q2d/rlgc_matrix.csv`. The existing 2024.2 native export
mapping uses PyAEDT 1.3.0 `Q2d.export_matrix_data(problem_type="CG, RL")`.
This version-specific method reference does not set a default; requests select
the AEDT release explicitly as above. The artifact's primary result blocks are
the capacitance (C), conductance (G), inductance (L), and resistance (R)
matrices. Native coupling or Spice blocks may coexist in the same export, but
they are not additional primary result matrices.

The former `results/q2d/cg_matrix.csv`, `results/q2d/rl_matrix.csv`, and
normalized `results/q2d/matrices.csv` outputs are superseded and absent from
new-run manifests; SCGSim does not emit compatibility copies. `resolve_results()`
binds the single native artifact, `result.primary_csv` points to it, and
`result.physics_results()` exposes its parsed primary C/G/L/R rows without
creating a second artifact.

Resolution fails closed unless the connected AEDT/PyAEDT versions, declared
setup and `LastAdaptive` solution, frequency, per-unit-length units, conductor
order, and every primary matrix value match the sealed run and are finite.

## Q3D extraction and Region-ground contract {#q3d-extraction-and-region-ground-candidate}

The current Q3D request uses only `scgsim.aedt.q3d.v3`. A `Q3dSpec` carries
the `PreparedSgbModel` AEDT imports and one `Q3dNetSpec` per Net of that model
([Q3D on the SGB model](#q3d-sgb-model)); it declares no bodies, GDS import or
per-piece binding. The remaining project, Net, run-control, Region and
extraction controls described below retain their existing meanings.

`Q3dNetSpec.name` is the Net's AEDT name (its sanitised ID) and
`Q3dNetSpec.object_names` names the model's conductor objects of that Net, so
one Net may own several objects and every conductor object belongs to exactly
one Net. A Net carries no source or sink.

A Q3D request extracts capacitance and conductance only: Q3D creates only the
capacitance/conductance setup and seals and resolves exactly the native
`results/q3d/c_matrix.csv`; a saved AC-RL or DC block, an `ACRLConv`
convergence block or an AC-RL matrix file is refused. AC/RL is not available on the SGB model; it is designed again, with sources and sinks of their own, in
[issue #265](https://github.com/NCUPHY-LTLab/scgsim/issues/265).

`Q3dSpec.grounded_region_net` is either `null`, retaining the open formulation,
or non-empty text naming a new SCGSim-created, dedicated Region-enclosure
`GroundNet`. The generated name must not collide with any declared physical
net. This is a capacitance/conductance construction and makes no DC or AC-RL
return-path claim.

For a grounded Region, SCGSim creates exactly six PEC `ThinConductor` sheets
from the six native faces of the AEDT object named `Region`. The sheets remain
separate edge-touching geometry objects and are assigned only to the generated
Region-enclosure net; SCGSim does not unite them or add a physical bridge.
Declared physical `Ground` nets and their native object assignments remain
unchanged.

PyAEDT 1.3.0 public APIs remain the construction path. After the pre-solve
project save, the runtime calls AEDT's native `ValidateDesign`. The receipt
seals successful validation together with the generated net and sheet
assignments. It also binds the exact `+X`, `-X`, `+Y`, `-Y`, `+Z`, and `-Z`
directions; pre-sheet Region object and face identities, centers, and normals;
separately read-back final Region faces; created sheet object identities and
names; thin-conductor boundary names; Region bounds; generated net identity;
and native net and boundary assignment readback.

The resolver requires exact equality between sealed and native readback
assignments, proves that generated and declared physical-net assignments are
disjoint, and verifies that declared physical `Ground` assignments remain
unchanged. Missing, repeated, mismatched, non-native, or unsuccessful validation
evidence rejects the run.
The same native Region and boundary evidence is read again after the final
post-solve project save before it becomes receipt-authoritative.

AEDT Region history expands again when model sheets are placed on its faces.
SCGSim therefore snapshots the Region's native faces, creates the six sheets
there, and rebuilds the final native Region with zero additional offset. The
final Region keeps the model's `VACUUM_REGION` bounds and the imported Region's
material; the receipt records this zero-offset finalization explicitly.

There is no compatibility fallback, physical bridge, or unite path.

### Q3D on the SGB model {#q3d-sgb-model}

Q3D models the geometry Palace meshes (issue #67). The structured frontend is
`prepare_q3d_from_geometry(snapshot: GeometryPlanSnapshot, *,
aedt_version: str, modeling, output_dir, project_name, design_name,
net_types: Mapping[str, Literal["Signal", "Ground"]],
physical_ground_nets: Sequence[str],
run_control: MatrixRunControl | None = None,
resources: AedtResources | None = None) -> HandoffPlan`. It builds the plan's
SGB model with `prepare_sgb_model` and returns a portable v3 handoff for C/G:

1. `modeling="solid"` builds Route C (conductor solids); `"thin_film"` builds
   Route A (conductor sheets) with its finite bodies retained as solids. The
   STEP leaves out the vacuum; Q3D's Region is the plan's `VACUUM_REGION` box,
   so a plan without `GeometryPlan.set_vacuum_region(...)` is refused and the
   request has no Region padding.
2. `net_types` gives every Net of the model its Q3D type, keyed by Net ID, and
   must name exactly the model's Nets. `physical_ground_nets` records which
   Nets are physically ground (`PreparedSgbModel.ground_net_ids`),
   independently of their Q3D type.
3. Each Net becomes one `Q3dNetSpec` over the model's conductor objects of that
   Net: the guard's conductor solids and, in Route A, the conductor sheets
   rebuilt as objects. Nets whose IDs become one AEDT name are refused.
4. The materials are the stack's records of the materials the model's volumes
   name. A Route C conductor solid is `pec`; a dielectric takes its stack
   material; the Region takes the vacuum's.

The handoff carries the model's STEP, BREP, sidecar and guard in its `model/`
folder, listed in the manifest after `aedt_spec.json`, and its receipt source
binds `sgb_model_sha256` and `sgb_model_files`. On the AEDT machine the request
is decoded against that folder and every file is checked again. A request that
declares natively built `bodies` or `region_padding_um`, or a receipt source
without the model's keys, is refused with the reason (decision 6); there is no
conversion from an earlier Q3D request.

The runtime imports the guarded STEP into an empty Q3D design
(`import_sgb_model`): the objects must be exactly the guard's solids, every
face is matched to its planned face, the materials and the Region are created
and read back. In Route A it first rebuilds each conductor-sheet group
(`SHEET`) as one sheet object, copied from the face it lies on and named by
the group, and makes it a PEC `ThinConductor` of the film's physical thickness
from the stack layer (`PreparedSgbModel.sheet_thickness_um`), read back. It then assigns each request Net with its Q3D type over its
objects and reads each Net's objects back.

Result reading requires the receipt's geometry to carry the model identity and
the guard's solids, its Nets to be the request's, and its Region
to be the model's `VACUUM_REGION` box within the readback tolerance.

#### Q3D native build-only execution

Q3D v3 has an opt-in native build-only operation using the existing
`python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --execute --prepare-only`
entrypoint. It follows the same model import, material and Net assignment,
Region and setup creation/readback, project save, and owned Desktop release as
the solver path. It does not call native `Analyze`, create a solver mesh, solve,
or export matrices or convergence data. The receipt records
`status="native_preparation_only"`, `solver_invoked=false`, and
`resources.status="not_used_prepare_only"`; the saved AEDT project is the only
native output. This execution consumes the one-shot handoff, so a later solve
requires a newly prepared handoff. The strict `resolve_results` entrypoint
continues to require a completed solver result; it does not resolve a
preparation-only receipt as a result. Normal Q3D
`--execute` behavior is unchanged.

The v3 handoff's allowed paths are `run_aedt.sh`, `aedt_spec.json`, the
model's four files under `model/`, and the three metadata files; the
manifest's `members` sequence omits its own path and preserves the order and
hashes of the other files, nine allowed paths and eight records.

#### Q3D user-requested Stop/Abort and save

SCGSim exposes two mutually exclusive operations:
`scgsim.aedt.request_q3d_stop_and_save(handoff)` requests Clean Stop, allowing
the current pass to finish, while
`scgsim.aedt.request_q3d_abort_and_save(handoff)` requests Abort of current
work. The current receipt uses one `termination` carrier with an explicit
mode; it does not add a clean-only `normal_stop` alias. Existing sealed
receipts and reader rules remain unchanged, with no conversion adapter. Their
direct CLI actions are:

```sh
python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --stop-and-save
python -m scgsim.aedt.run --handoff <run-dir>/metadata/aedt_handoff_metadata.json --abort-and-save
```

Use either request action instead of `--execute`; the two modes are mutually
exclusive with each other and with `--prepare-only`, analyze/solve controls,
and resource overrides such as `--cores` or `--ram-limit-percent`. Each mode
uses the same private control ledger and stable lock. A requester is a separate
local Linux process bound to the exact active transaction: Desktop creation
identity (start time, boot identity, and UID), PID, port, full project, design,
setup, runtime/input identity, and nonce. It never attaches to a default/latest
Desktop. Repeating the committed mode is idempotent; a conflicting mode is
refused without another native RPC.
Unsupported platforms fail before Desktop attachment.

On Linux, execute-mode stop-managed Q3D refuses PyAEDT documentation mode
(`PYAEDT_DOC_GENERATION`) before creating a Desktop. That mode overrides the
Desktop close flags required for exclusive transaction ownership.

The recorder retains the blocking Analyze. Clean Stop calls PyAEDT
`Desktop.stop_simulations(clean_stop=True)` (native
`oDesktop.StopSimulations(True)`); Abort calls it with
`clean_stop=False` to interrupt current work. The receipt records mode/intent,
RPC outcome, and raw native response separately. A returned RPC is not an
acknowledgment: its response is uninterpreted and proves neither interruption
nor success. Neither the Analyze return/exception nor the Stop/Abort RPC
proves native inactivity or successful saving.

After Analyze settles, the recorder closes admission and makes one native
`odesktop.AreThereSimulationsRunning(True)` observation. Its `True` argument
includes running and pending simulations; only native `False` confirms
inactivity. Active, unknown, or unavailable native state, or uncertain
control-ledger closure/read/write/readback, fails the workflow and defers
Save/export with
`attempted=false` and `native_not_confirmed_inactive`, and preserves the owned
Desktop through non-closing detach with `release.ok=false`. It does not
fabricate a committed intent,
`normal_stop_saved`, or `abort_saved` status, write a post-release seal, or
clean up the preserved Desktop automatically. Later owner action remains
explicit.

With confirmed inactivity and known control-ledger state, the recorder first
attempts the explicit transaction Save; a preparation-time save cannot satisfy
this requirement. Requested available completed-result matrices and native
convergence exports are then attempted and recorded independently. Any raw
native files actually produced remain retained even if export/readback parsing
fails, with availability and errors recorded truthfully. Optional outputs do
not prove that an interrupted pass completed or promise recovery/completeness.
The owned Desktop is closed/released only if this explicit Save succeeds. If
Save fails, the receipt is `FAILED`; the recorder performs a non-closing
detach with `release.ok=false` and reason `save_failed`. The project and
Desktop remain preserved, actual recoverable artifacts and ownership/error
evidence are retained, and no post-release seal or automatic cleanup occurs.
A successful release is required before sealing the actual released
identities.

The mode-specific `normal_stop_saved` and `abort_saved` statuses require the
committed matching intent, returned RPC, Analyze returning true, confirmed
native inactivity, successful explicit Save and Desktop release, and
post-release seal. They describe only the finalized Stop/Abort-and-save
workflow, not physics completion or proof that the request caused termination;
Analyze can finish naturally. Analyze false/exception remains the primary
failure with causality unknown; control-mode/intent, ACF restoration, RPC,
Save/export, and release errors remain separately recorded. Optional export
errors do not define the Stop/Abort-save workflow status or make it a completed
solver result.
Strict `resolve_results()` and Report behavior remain unchanged, with no new
partial-result reader or Report API. No polling, wait loop, additional Stop/Abort, retry, or automatic cleanup is performed.
These controls apply only to new executions registered by this runtime; old runs are
not retrofitted. Ordinary Q3D without request intent, HFSS, Q2D, Eigenmode EPR,
and non-Linux solver flows are unchanged. The Eigenmode EPR
no-automatic-partial-save rule remains unchanged.

The v3 handoff's allowed paths are `run_aedt.sh`, `aedt_spec.json`, the
model's four files under `model/`, and the three metadata files; the
manifest's `members` sequence omits its own path and preserves the order and
hashes of the other files, nine allowed paths and eight records.

## Eigenmode saved fields and Surface-EPR direction

HFSS Eigenmode runs on the SGB model Palace meshes (issue #67).
`EigenmodeSim.prepare_handoff()` builds it with `prepare_sgb_model()` from the
plan, its junctions, lumped RLCs and Surface-EPR specs, and writes the handoff
that carries it; `EigenmodeSim.prepared_model` is then the model in that
handoff. Where AEDT runs, the request is read against the handoff folder, the
model's four files are checked again, and the Eigenmode design is made in this
order:

1. `import_sgb_model()` imports the guarded STEP, matches every face to its
   planned face, rebuilds the free faces, realizes the materials and the
   Region, and assigns Perfect E, the junction Lumped RLCs and the generic
   RLCs;
2. for an EPR request, one non-model sheet per selected Surface-EPR row and
   one voltage sheet per junction are copied from the imported faces;
3. the setup is created;
4. the EPR expressions are compiled from the sidecar rows and loaded once,
   and a requested expression cache is submitted;
5. the project is saved and the setup is read back.

The receipt's geometry record is the import record: each planned solid and its
AEDT object, the imported copies of each planned face, the rebuilt sheets,
every assignment, the selection sheets and the model identity. Result reading
refuses a receipt whose model identity, guard solids or bound file hashes are
not those of the request's model.

`EprAnalysisRequest.surface_epr_groups` selects sidecar Surface-EPR groups
(`None`: every group); `junction_ids` and `bulk_domain_ids` select the
reported junctions and domains, while every domain and junction stays in the
normalization. Surface EPR is declared with `EigenmodeSim.set_surface_epr(specs)`,
Palace's specs by interface type. Their inset margins become bands of the
model, and each row is integrated over all of its faces, sidewalls included.

A saved analysis (`analyze_epr(model=...)`) copies the saved project and
rebinds it by name: the guard's solids, the Region and every row and junction
sheet its expressions read must be in the saved design, and the saved
solution must name the same model identity. `surface_field_selectors` are
keyed by the same groups: `surface` reads a row's field on its sheet
(`EnterSurface`), `adjacent` just off it (`EnterAdjacentSurface`); the area
is the sheet's either way. A handoff, saved solution or receipt of the native
builder is refused (issue #67 decision 6).

Each required field quantity is evaluated in an explicitly bound setup,
`LastAdaptive` solution, mode, frequency, phase, and excitation context. That
context is read back with the value: a saved expression name or expression
digest alone is not solution identity because an unevaluated calculator stack
can follow later context changes.

### Mode binding and pass cache

Eigenmode postprocessing uses a complete native-order source vector. A numeric
control vector selects one entry with the dimensionless relative weight `1`
and sets every other entry to `0`; phase is explicit for every entry. These are
native `EigenPeakElectricField` source controls, not a measurement or assertion
of `1 V/m`. The cache-oriented form instead creates native postprocessing
variables, feeds their names to the same source magnitudes, and supplies a
concrete one-hot variable assignment for each calculation context. The path
neither calls `GetAllSources` as a prerequisite nor passes `Mode` as a
calculator intrinsic. It submits both forms through native `EditSources`, reads
back the persisted numeric or symbolic source entries, the native
postprocessing-variable values, and the solution context, then evaluates
discriminating local integrals for modes 1 and 2 before restoring mode 1. These
variables are postprocessing state only. They are not design variations, and
their amplitudes must not become an independent Cartesian variation space.

This mode check is distinct from adaptive-pass caching. The EPR runtime
compiles the complete cache item set and submits it in one setup edit; repeated
enable calls are not assumed to append. With no expression-convergence request,
SCGSim submits every primitive item with `IsConvergence=False`; this describes
the submitted settings. After saving, SCGSim records the raw convergence fields
present in each saved cache item and lists absent fields as unavailable. It
does not infer `false` or substitute submitted values when a field is absent.
Earlier records marked `NOT_VERIFIED_SERIALIZED_OMISSION` are not
retroactively enriched.
Saved settings describe configuration, not proof that AEDT used them to control
a solve. A cache item is identified by its namespaced definition plus bound
context, never by a display title alone. Multi-face quantities use a verified
native face list or an explicit sum of individually bound faces.

#### Independent expression-cache convergence targets

`ExpressionCacheConvergenceSet(controls=(...))` carries a nonempty ordered
collection of unit `ExpressionCacheConvergence` controls. The public setter and
preparation helper accept either a unit or a collection. A collection serializes
as `scgsim.aedt.hfss-eigenmode-epr.v4`; a unit control serializes as V3 and a
request without one as V2. Duplicate target/mode pairs are rejected.

```python
from scgsim.aedt import (
    ExpressionCacheConvergence, ExpressionCacheConvergenceSet, NormalizedSurfaceEprTotal,
)

sim.set_expression_cache_convergence(ExpressionCacheConvergenceSet(controls=tuple(
    ExpressionCacheConvergence(
        mode=mode_index,
        target=NormalizedSurfaceEprTotal(interface, "requested_margin", margin_um),
        criterion=criterion_percent,
        use_relative_convergence=True,
    )
    for interface in interface_kinds
)))
```

The caller supplies `mode_index`, `margin_um`, `criterion_percent` and
`interface_kinds`. The EPR request must include each target's prepared margin
evaluation. Each interface is an independent normalized total with its own
native criterion; the interfaces are never summed into one convergence target. Caller frequency, minimum,
maximum and consecutive-pass settings remain unchanged. [AEDT 2024.2 documents
that Eigenmode also requires frequency convergence in addition to its enabled
expression criteria](https://ansyshelp.ansys.com/public/Views/Secured/Electronics/v242/en/Subsystems/HFSS/Content/HFSS/SpecifyingExpressionsforAdaptiveConvergence.htm).
This documented conjunction is the requested native rule, not an observed
combined-convergence result. Completion or frequency convergence alone does not
establish that all targets converged; missing native stop evidence stays missing.
Near-zero native percentage behavior is not replaced with an epsilon or absolute
criterion.

Each active item retains its control identity, expression/cache identity, mode,
requested criterion and separately observed saved criterion fields. Native
`Pass=All` cache rows retain their returned coordinates, values and missingness
for each target. Configuration readback parses the exact saved project with
PyAEDT's pinned, uncached `load_entire_aedt_file` reader, selects the bound HFSS
design and setup, and records that file's hash. It does not use `setup.props` or
the application project-properties cache. Requested native fields, actual saved
fields, raw representation differences and unavailable fields remain separate.
Saved frequency/pass controls are recorded alongside them. Matching setup
configuration does not establish that a target met its criterion.

Per-pass field retention is unknown; LastAdaptive saved-field identity is
separate. No offline percentage delta is fabricated.

#### Selecting an expression-cache convergence target {#epr-expression-cache-convergence}

`EigenmodeSim.set_expression_cache_convergence(control)` replaces the current
selection; repeated calls do not accumulate controls. Omit the setting or pass
`None` to select no expression-convergence criterion, pass one
`ExpressionCacheConvergence` for a singleton, or pass an
`ExpressionCacheConvergenceSet` containing the chosen subset of targets. Routine
EPR computation and reporting do not automatically enable convergence criteria.
Each selected control's mode must also be selected by the configured
`EprAnalysisRequest`.

For the singleton case, the setter enables one expression-cache item for a
caller-selected mode and explicit criterion, and the handoff records that
setting in `scgsim.aedt.hfss-eigenmode-epr.v3`. A collection uses V4 as described
above; a request without a control uses V2. With no control selected, SCGSim authors no auxiliary expression and
submits the same non-converging primitive cache items as before. The low-level
`prepare_hfss_eigenmode_from_geometry()` requires both `aedt_version` and
`modeling`, and accepts the same `expression_convergence` argument.

Native frequency convergence controls remain separate and unchanged. AEDT
requires those frequency criteria together with only the explicitly selected,
enabled expression criteria; unselected computed EPR quantities are not added
to that conjunction.

`criterion` is passed to AEDT without scaling. With
`use_relative_convergence=True`, it is the native **Max Percent Delta** in
percent units (`5.0` means 5%); with `False`, it is the native **Max Delta** in
the expression's units. SCGSim does not convert a fraction to a percentage.
See the [AEDT 2024 R2 expression convergence reference](https://ansyshelp.ansys.com/public/Views/Secured/Electronics/v242/en/Subsystems/Circuit/Content/HFSS/SpecifyingExpressionsforAdaptiveConvergence.htm).

The normalized target selects one interface, evaluation, and margin, and sums
the prepared owner groups selected by the EPR request. It uses the existing
peak-phasor surface-energy coefficients and divides by the existing model-wide
normalization: electric energy over every solution domain plus capacitive
energy for every model junction. Output filters do not narrow that denominator.
Surface energy is not added to the denominator. `unmasked_baseline` and a
`requested_margin` of zero remain distinct evaluations.

```python
from scgsim.aedt import (
    ExpressionCacheConvergence,
    NormalizedSurfaceEprTotal,
)

# The configured EPR request already includes mode 1 and an MS evaluation
# at the requested 0.5 µm margin.
sim.set_expression_cache_convergence(
    ExpressionCacheConvergence(
        mode=1,
        target=NormalizedSurfaceEprTotal(
            interface_kind="MS",
            evaluation_kind="requested_margin",
            margin_um=0.5,
        ),
        criterion=5.0,
        use_relative_convergence=True,
    )
)
```

For a caller-authored target, `NativeExpressionDefinition` carries a label and
native Fields Calculator operation sequence. The same batch compiler creates
and loads its definition with the rest of the EPR expressions; an existing
native-name collision fails preparation. This example integrates the electric
field norm over the native `Region` object, in the units of that integral:

```python
from scgsim.aedt import ExpressionCacheConvergence, NativeExpressionDefinition

sim.set_expression_cache_convergence(
    ExpressionCacheConvergence(
        mode=2,
        target=NativeExpressionDefinition(
            name="region_electric_integral",
            operations=(
                "Fundamental_Quantity('E')",
                "Operation('Conj')",
                "Fundamental_Quantity('E')",
                "Operation('Dot')",
                "Operation('Real')",
                "EnterVolume('Region')",
                "Operation('VolumeValue')",
                "Operation('Integrate')",
            ),
        ),
        criterion=5.0,
        use_relative_convergence=True,
    )
)
```

The label is part of expression identity; the compiler assigns the native
expression name. The custom operation sequence must be valid for the prepared
native design. Both targets add an auxiliary cache item for the selected mode,
with `IsConvergence`, `UseRelativeConvergence`, `MaxConvergenceDelta`, and
`MaxConvergeValue` submitted from the requested control. Other modes' cache
items remain non-converging. Saved-setup readback records the raw fields
present for each cache item and separately names unavailable fields; it does
not fill omissions from the request. Auxiliary values and cache titles stay
in the existing `adaptive-mode-history.json` cache collection; they are not
decoded as one of the primitive EPR integrals and do not alter EPR
raw-integral completeness. Each cache item keeps its selected mode's existing
one-hot intrinsic context.

The submission record starts with
`native_readback.status="PENDING_SAVED_SETUP_READBACK"`. After the existing
save, `serialized_readback.convergence_fields` records per-item raw `values`
and an `unavailable` list. That saved configuration still does not establish
that the solver applied the criterion or that it changed the adaptive stop;
those outcomes require an actual target-run observation.

### Public EPR surface {#public-epr-candidate-surface}

The public HFSS Eigenmode entries are `EigenmodeSim` (with `set_plan`,
`set_eigenmode`, `set_surface_epr`, `add_junction`, `add_lumped_rlc` and
`set_epr_request`), `prepare_sgb_model()` with
`prepare_hfss_eigenmode_from_geometry(model=...)`, and `analyze_epr(model=...)`
for a saved solution. All of them take the one `PreparedSgbModel` of an SGB
build; there is no planar Eigenmode preparation. HFSS Driven Terminal takes
the same `PreparedSgbModel` ([its route](#hfss-driven-terminal-sgb)).

#### Automatic rectangular junction partition {#aedt-automatic-junction-partition}

For this AEDT path, the authored rectangular junction sheet is partitioned into
two terminal-side conductor ends and one full-authored-width central RLC
rectangle. The complete original inductance and capacitance remain assigned
only to that central rectangle. The final RLC rectangle must have exactly two
opposite terminal-contact edges; the authored sheet may contact terminals on
all four edges. The A-to-B direction and axis come from the authored rectangle
and port direction. SCGSim does not swap terminals to make a partition fit.
The contract does not add manual cut positions, a fixed 50-nm clearance,
narrower-width fallback, or a general rectangle optimizer.

The maximum means the longest valid central rectangle only within a verified
clear interval for this rectangular topology; it is not a claim about every
possible layout. Closed contact with either terminal includes area, segment,
and point contact. Coordinates use the authored rectangle's local frame and
its A-to-B direction. Let `L` be the largest `s` coordinate where the source
contacts terminal A and `U` the smallest where it contacts terminal B; the
interval must satisfy `L < U`.
The full-width corridor, including its side boundaries, must be clear of other
metal. The A end may contact only terminal A and the B end only terminal B;
cross-terminal or third-net contact is rejected. If these preconditions do
not hold, the implementation reports unsupported topology/search assumptions
rather than universal infeasibility.

Search uses the source-local DBU `h` recorded with the partition evidence. It
must be finite and positive; missing precision fails instead of guessing. Let
`s_min` be the lower source-local bound; a candidate coordinate is derived as
`s_min + k*h` from an integer local index.
The algorithm checks each aligned interval endpoint and the nearest strictly
interior grid point on each side (at most two candidates per side), then picks
the smallest valid A index and largest valid B index, requiring `a < b`.
This constant-size search relies on the verified clear corridor: moving a cut
there adds a full-width strip without changing the topology or contacts behind
the cut. It does not scan the DBU grid or resnap derived coordinates to a
Cartesian GDS grid. The recorded indices, local coordinates, frame, precision,
Boolean output, and deviations keep index arithmetic distinct from the
geometry kernel's separate precision. Boolean collapse or topology change is a
numerical geometry failure, not proof that all cuts are invalid.

Native readback compares coordinates componentwise with one absolute tolerance
of `1e-5 µm` and zero relative tolerance. The same policy covers the junction
midpoint, source/native vertex and edge coordinates, straightness, Z/extrusion,
lumped-line coordinates, and contact checks. It compares returned geometry
without snapping to the DBU, moving the model, or changing source or cache
identity; observed values and deviations remain readback evidence. This
practical SCGSim allowance for CAD/API variation is 1% of the contextual 1 nm
source DBU. It is not an AEDT accuracy guarantee. Contact claims are
limited to this readback resolution, so a sub-resolution gap or contact cannot
be proven absent. Topology, holes, assignments, and actual gaps, shorts,
overlaps, and curvature remain subject to the existing checks. Inductance and
capacitance use their own dimensionally appropriate value comparisons, not this
length tolerance.

If native edge readback fails, the existing run receipt's `error` field
preserves the `RuntimeError` text. It distinguishes invalid or mismatched
midpoint and native-length checks, with per-condition codes and residuals,
edge/face identifiers, endpoint coordinates, observed and expected midpoint,
native length, straight-line chord, and the `model_units` value (`um`). Treat
its coordinate values as consumer-private run evidence.
A failed length/chord or midpoint comparison is a readback inconsistency, not
proof that the CAD edge is curved. PyAEDT's [`EdgePrimitive.length` API](https://aedt.docs.pyansys.com/version/stable/API/_autosummary/ansys.aedt.core.modeler.cad.elements_3d.EdgePrimitive.length.html)
documents lengths in model units for edges with two vertices and `False`
otherwise; the installed 1.3 wrapper converts `GetEdgeLength` to `float` and
returns `False` if that call raises. The API gives no numerical precision
bound. SCGSim's `1e-5 µm` coordinate policy is not a guarantee of AEDT
edge-length accuracy.

Extrusion-side association uses native face-edge incidence rather than
proximity-only interval projection. PyAEDT's [`FacePrimitive.edges` API](https://aedt.docs.pyansys.com/version/stable/API/_autosummary/ansys.aedt.core.modeler.cad.elements_3d.FacePrimitive.edges.html)
returns the face's `EdgePrimitive` objects through `GetEdgeIDsFromFace`.
SCGSim associates each raw horizontal side edge with a cap edge only when both
